acquisition_method: Mass spectrometry data was acquired in a data directed manner for 90 min in positive mode.
alkylation_reagent: After shearing, samples were alkylated by the addition of 8 µL of 500 mM iodoacetamide (Sigma, I1149) and incubated for 30 min in the dark.
cleavage_agent: In-column digest was performed by adding 25 µL of a 0.8 µg/µL trypsin solution (proteomics grade trypsin; Promega, V5111) in 50 mM TEAB pH 8.0 in accordance with the manufacturer’s protocol for 1-hour digestion.
collision_energy: The MS2 Resolution was set to 30,000, with an AGC target of 2e5, a maximum fill time of 45 ms, isolation window of 1.3Th and a collision energy of 28.
fragmentation_method: inferred: The text states 'collision energy of 28' and uses a 'Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer'. HCD is the standard fragmentation method for Q Exactive instruments when 'collision energy' is specified, distinct from CID which is typical of ion traps or older instruments, and ETD/EThcD which require specific precursor charge states and are not described here.
ionization_type: inferred: The method uses 'directly inject onto the analytical column... at a flow rate of 300 nL/min'. 300 nL/min is a nano-flow rate, and Q Exactive HF instruments in this context are equipped with a nano-electrospray source. While 'ESI' is implied, 'nanoESI' is the more precise description of the ionization interface given the flow rates.
labeling: inferred: No isobaric labels (TMT, iTRAQ) or metabolic labels (SILAC) are mentioned in the sample preparation or analysis sections. Quantification is performed via 'BayesENproteomics' using peptide intensities, which is a label-free approach.
mass_analyzer: inferred: The instrument is a 'Q Exactive HF', which is an Orbitrap-based mass spectrometer.
reduction_concentration: We then added 75 µL of a 50 mM TEAB, 5% SDS, 10 M urea, 13.3 mM DTT (pH 7.5) solution to the 25 µL sample, after it had cooled to room temperature to avoid deamination, to create a final volume of 100 µL of 50 mM TEAB, 5% SDS, 7.5 M urea, 10 mT DTT (pH 7.5).
reduction_reagent: We then added 75 µL of a 50 mM TEAB, 5% SDS, 10 M urea, 13.3 mM DTT (pH 7.5) solution to the 25 µL sample, after it had cooled to room temperature to avoid deamination, to create a final volume of 100 µL of 50 mM TEAB, 5% SDS, 7.5 M urea, 10 mT DTT (pH 7.5).

instrument.evidence: coupled to a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher).
